## (2) Approaches message

Before the approaches, here are the implicit dependencies I could not check. Each one is carried as unverified:

- **The CSV serializer.** Lookup: read src/export/csv.ts. Result: not run here; the gather draft says it exists and reuses table column definitions.
- **The table column definitions as the source of visible columns, in table order.** Lookup: read the reports table's column definitions. Result: not run here; the gather draft asserts it.
- **Paging that can fetch a 10k-row report within the 60s row.** Lookup: read the reports paging code and time a 10k-row fetch. Result: not run here; the gather draft asserts the target is supported, with no measurement cited.

I recommend **Approach A**. The two candidates differ on where the export is assembled: in the browser from what already exists, or on a server as a new job.

**A) Reuse-only: client-side export through the existing serializer (recommended).**
- An Export CSV button sits beside the report title.
- It takes the table's visible column definitions in table order.
- It pages through the existing reports paging path to collect every row.
- It hands the rows to src/export/csv.ts and triggers a download.

Nothing new is introduced beyond the button and its handler. The serializer and column definitions stay the single source of truth.

The trade-off is that the 10k-row/60s row depends on client-side paging throughput, which is still unverified. A slow page size would show up only at measurement.

Removes: none
Adds: Export CSV button component beside the report title; export click handler wiring visible column definitions, paging, and src/export/csv.ts; a test for the button and the column order; a timed 10k-row export test
Pattern: follows the existing reuse of the table's column definitions in src/export/csv.ts. No second column list or serializer is created.

**B) Drop the assumption that export is a synchronous in-browser download: a server-side export job.**
- The button requests an export.
- A server job builds the CSV from the same column set and returns a download link when it is done.

This drops the ask's implicit assumption that the browser does the work. It would also be the natural base for emailed exports later. The cost is several new parts:
- an endpoint
- job handling
- a server-side copy of the visible-column choice

It also adds a second place that decides which columns export. That is a split of the column contract src/export/csv.ts currently owns.

Removes: none
Adds: export endpoint; export job runner; server-side use of the CSV serializer; job-status/download link in the UI; Export CSV button beside the report title; endpoint, job, and 10k-row timing tests
Pattern: cuts across src/export/csv.ts's client-side reuse of the table column definitions by needing the visible-column set reproduced server-side. The gather draft identifies no existing server export location to follow.

**What would flip the recommendation to B:**
- the paging lookup or the 10k-row timing shows client-side export cannot finish in under 60s, or
- the phase-2 answer puts emailed exports in this repo (option A), since that needs a server-side job anyway.
